preemption.title: Workspace Preemption Switch
preemption.description: This page is visible only to platform admins. It controls whether, within each Workspace, tasks in a higher priority class can evict tasks in a lower priority class when the quota is used up.
preemption.confirmOffDesc: After it is turned off, tasks in this Workspace only queue and never preempt.
preemption.confirmOnDesc: ⚠️ After it is turned on, higher-priority tasks may evict running lower-priority tasks (a preempted training job rolls back to its checkpoint).
preemption.when: When does preemption happen? All three conditions below must be met at the same time; if any one is not met, it will not happen:
preemption.cond1: The preemption switch of this Workspace is on.
preemption.cond2: The compute quota of this Workspace is used up.
preemption.cond3: A task in a higher priority class is queued in the same Workspace.
preemption.boundary1: Preemption only takes effect inside a single Workspace; Workspaces do not affect each other.
preemption.boundary2: Preemption evicts the task's containers, but the task itself is kept. Its queue status becomes "Evicted" and it then re-enters the queue.
preemption.boundary3: A preempted training job is re-queued automatically, and it can resume only if checkpoint fault tolerance is configured on the training side.
preemption.boundary4: When an inference service or dev instance is preempted, the online service or user session is interrupted.
preemption.advice: Recommendation: Before turning on preemption, confirm that the training jobs in this Workspace have checkpoint fault tolerance.
preemption.readOnlyDesc: Only platform admins can change the preemption switch of a Workspace.

priorityLabels.title: Priority Class
priorityLabels.description: This page is visible only to platform admins. Priority classes are a dictionary shared by all Workspaces on the platform; every task picks its class from here.
priorityLabels.tip1: The weight is a relative value (0-100) and only determines the relative order.
priorityLabels.tip2: A larger weight means higher priority, which shows up in two ways: (1) when tasks queue, tasks with a larger weight go first; (2) in Workspaces where the preemption switch is on, tasks in a higher-weight class can evict running tasks in a lower-weight class.
priorityLabels.tip3: Changing a class value only affects tasks submitted afterwards; tasks that are already running or queued keep the value snapshot from when they were submitted and are not recalculated.
priorityLabels.tip4: This page only manages the class dictionary itself. Changing the class of a specific task is not done here: a Workspace admin or platform admin does it on the "Task Overview" page of that Workspace by clicking the pencil icon in the task row's priority class column (queued tasks: the queue order is adjusted immediately; running tasks: the task restarts).
priorityLabels.readOnlyDesc: Only platform admins can add, edit, or delete priority classes.

resourceTemplates.title: Resource Template
resourceTemplates.description: This page manages the resource templates of the current Workspace (they are maintained per Workspace, so you see different templates when you switch Workspaces).
resourceTemplates.tip1: Dev instances, training jobs and inference services share one set of templates. When creating a task, users can only pick a template and cannot enter CPU / GPU / memory by hand.
resourceTemplates.tip2: All Workspace members can open and view this page; only Workspace admins or platform admins can create, edit, or delete templates. Regular members get read-only access.
resourceTemplates.selectWsHint: Resource templates are maintained per Workspace · pick a Workspace from the "Workspace" menu on the left first

form.name: Template name
form.efaTip: Used for the high-speed network (RDMA) of multi-node GPU training. Enter 0 for single-node jobs, dev instances and inference. The instance type must support EFA.

fsxQuota.title: FSx Quota
fsxQuota.titleTip: Storage quotas on the shared FSx, set per top-level directory (team). Creating a directory automatically assigns a gid + setgid permission + project quota; the usage of each directory vs. its quota is shown in real time below.
fsxQuota.exceedsCapacity: The total quota of {{projected}} GiB would exceed the FSx total capacity of {{total}} GiB (other directories already take up {{other}} GiB).

stats.usedTip: Sum of the actual usage of all directories (read via lfs quota).
stats.allocatedTip: Sum of the hard limits of all directories. If it exceeds the FSx total capacity, the quota is over-subscribed and this value turns yellow.

createForm.alert: The setgid permission and project id are assigned automatically by the backend. For the gid, you can reuse an existing team or leave it empty to create a new one.
createForm.namePattern: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens; must start with a letter or digit
createForm.nameExtra: Creates /<directory-name> under the FSx root, e.g. team-name
createForm.gidExtra: Reusing an existing gid = the new directory belongs to that team (shared group permissions); its quota is still counted separately. Leave empty to create a new team.
createForm.gidPlaceholder: Not selected = create a new team (gid assigned automatically)

fsxQuota.softHintValue: Soft-limit alert line = 80% of the hard limit ≈ {{soft}} GiB (usage above the soft limit triggers a yellow alert)
fsxQuota.softHintEmpty: Soft-limit alert line = 80% of the hard limit; usage above it triggers a yellow alert
